statements.t: Generally, we expect increases in market interest rates will increase our net interest income and net interest margin in future periods, while decreases in market interest rates may decrease our net interest income and net interest margin in future periods; however, this depends upon the timing and extent of both short-term and long-term interest rate fluctuations and may not always be the case.
The Company’s investment policy emphasizes safety of the principal, liquidity needs, expected returns, cash flow targets, and consistency with our interest rate risk management strategy.

As of September 30, 2026, management believed the current liquidity and available sources of liquidity are adequate to meet all of the reasonably foreseeable short-term and intermediate-term demands of the Holding Company, including the cash consideration of the pending Tri-County acquisition anticipated to be paid early in the first quarter of 2027 .
Management uses the discounted cash flow method to estimate expected credit losses for all loan categories, except for consumer loans where the weighted average remaining maturity method is utilized.

Management leverages economic projections from a reputable third party to form its economic forecasts with a reversion to historical averages for periods beyond a reasonable and supportable forecast period.

estimates.name: Allowance for Credit Losses
estimates.t: The allowance for credit losses reflects an estimate of lifetime expected credit losses.

estimates.name: Fair Value of Assets Acquired and Liabilities Assumed in Business Combinations
estimates.t: Under the acquisition method of accounting, assets acquired and liabilities assumed are recorded at their estimated fair value on the acquisition date.
